Chapter 1 'Phonology' (pp. 1-68) per the table of contents covers inventory, phonemic contrasts, phonetic description of vowels and consonants, vowel sequences and consonant clusters only; no suprasegmental/stress/accent section; a full-text search for stress/accent the (poor) scanned layer for stress/accent = 0. The 'Supra segmental' heading (p.96) lists only 'Nasalization: /v~/'; a separate 'Vowel length' paragraph (p.95: 'Length is predictable in the monosyllabic words only.. length in monosyllabic words contrasts with non-monosyllabic ones'); then consonant distribution, allophones, h-loss, diphthongs, clusters, morphology. Introduction sec. 3.3 'Phonology' (pp. xlvi-xlvii) gives consonant chart, five vowels, long vowels ('can also occur as long vowels'), nasalized vowels, diphthongs ai oi au, syllable types V.CCVC, then: 'For more information on the phonology of Adiwasi Oriya see: Kotia Oriya Phonemic Summary, 1974, by Uwe Gustafsson.' [...] All monosyllabic ‘utterdnces carry the highest degree of stress.
tone.locator: Index (front matter) entry for ch. 1 Phonemics, and Section I Grammar, ch. 1 Phonemics, 'II. Suprasegmental Phonemes' sections 3.1 Nasalization - 3.4 Stress, p. 38-39
tone.n_tones: 0 (no tone/pitch phoneme in the suprasegmental inventory)
tone.says: Ch. 1 Phonemics gives a closed inventory of suprasegmental phonemes - nasalization, length, juncture and stress (stress 'has phonemic value on a very limited number of words.. as it is predictable'; monosyllables carry the highest stress) - and posits no tone or pitch phoneme anywhere; pitch is mentioned only for song performance and clause-final intonation contours in the Texts section. I.e. Desia is described as non-tonal by enumeration of its suprasegmentals.
